title: DIR-093: Comprehensive End-to-End UI/UX Forensic Audit & Enhancement Planning
spec:
# ANTIGRAVITY EXECUTIVE DIRECTIVE — DIR-093
## Comprehensive End-to-End UI/UX Forensic Audit & Enhancement Planning

**Target Project:** IME365 — Interview Made Easy  
**Required Workspace:** `D:\xampp\htdocs\IME365`  
**Directive ID:** `DIR-093`  
**Priority:** P0 — Critical  
**Mode:** PLAN ONLY — Read-Only Investigation  
**Status:** ISSUED — Awaiting Forensic Audit & Plan Submission  
**Execution Authority:** Inspection and planning only. Implementation is not authorised in this phase.

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE MANDATE

Conduct a comprehensive, evidence-driven, end-to-end forensic audit of the entire IME365 application to identify and plan the resolution of every material UI/UX defect, missing interface capability, incomplete user journey, visual inconsistency, broken interaction, misleading data presentation, navigation defect, accessibility violation, responsive-layout issue, and frontend-to-backend integration gap.

The objective is to produce an implementation plan capable of bringing IME365 to a **production-grade, enterprise-quality, 10/10 UI/UX standard**, while preserving existing functionality, established architecture, genuine platform data, Cuba Design System compliance, and all protected project invariants.

Do not restrict the investigation to the homepage, dashboard, currently visible pages, or previously reported issues. Discover the actual application structure and systematically investigate all accessible routes, nested routes, subpages, layouts, reusable components, modals, drawers, forms, menus, tables, charts, filters, notifications, empty states, loading states, error states, and cross-feature workflows.

Treat this as a platform-wide completeness and quality investigation, not a cosmetic redesign exercise.

**Mandatory outcome:** A repository-specific, dependency-aware, risk-ranked, implementation-ready plan grounded in verified source-code evidence. Generic recommendations without file-level references, reproducible findings, or measurable acceptance criteria are insufficient.

## 2. ABSOLUTE PLAN-MODE RESTRICTIONS

This directive authorises investigation and planning only.

### Permitted actions

- Verify the current workspace and repository identity.
- Inspect Git status, current branch, HEAD commit, tracked files, and existing diffs.
- Read source code, configuration, routing definitions, design tokens, tests, and existing documentation.
- Inspect existing screenshots and visual-reference assets.
- Trace frontend-to-backend contracts and data dependencies through existing source code.
- Use non-mutating repository inspection commands.
- Prepare an evidence-based implementation plan.
- Submit the plan using the mandatory Bridge command in Section 13.

### Prohibited actions

- Do not edit, create, delete, rename, move, or format project files.
- Do not modify application code, stylesheets, design tokens, configuration, documentation, tests, or generated assets.
- Do not execute migrations, database writes, seeders, application mutations, deployment operations, or other state-changing actions.
- Do not install or update packages, regenerate lockfiles, alter environment variables, or change system configuration.
- Do not switch branches, reset the repository, stash changes, clean the working tree, or discard existing user modifications.
- Do not commit, push, merge, rebase, or otherwise alter Git history.
- Do not start implementation, autonomous repair loops, or code-generation workflows.
- Do not run commands that generate or overwrite build artifacts during this phase.
- Do not claim that tests, builds, accessibility checks, browser workflows, or visual comparisons have passed unless they were actually executed and verified. No implementation-phase verification is authorised here.

If an inspection tool might modify files or external state, do not invoke it. Record the proposed validation step for the implementation phase instead.

**Plan-mode completion means that the investigation and plan submission are complete—not that the UI/UX defects have been fixed.**

## 3. PRE-FLIGHT REPOSITORY AND WORKSPACE VERIFICATION

Before investigating application behaviour, establish the actual repository identity.

Verify:

1. The active workspace resolves to `D:\xampp\htdocs\IME365`.
2. The directory is the intended IME365 repository rather than another project or nested checkout.
3. The active Git branch, full HEAD commit hash, and upstream configuration where available.
4. The working-tree status, including staged changes, unstaged changes, and untracked files.
5. Existing user modifications that must be preserved.
6. The frontend framework, package manager, build scripts, lint scripts, testing framework, routing system, and application entry points.
7. The actual frontend source directories and relevant backend/API integration locations.

If the workspace does not match the required path, stop the investigation before examining a different project as though it were the target. Report the mismatch and submit a plan only if the intended repository can be safely identified without modifying anything.

Record the repository baseline in the final plan. Do not assume that a clean working tree, a particular branch, or a previously reported commit exists.

## 4. NON-NEGOTIABLE PROJECT INVARIANTS

### 4.1 Protected CV template directory

**`src/cv-templates/` is strictly immutable.**

- Do not modify any file within this directory.
- Do not propose direct edits to these files as the implementation solution.
- Do not move, rename, regenerate, or reformat protected templates.
- Any future visual or integration enhancement must be implemented through permitted surrounding components, adapters, configuration, or rendering interfaces where architecturally appropriate.
- Establish the baseline Git diff and verify that the directory remains untouched throughout the authorised phase.

Required invariant:

`git diff -- src/cv-templates/` must remain empty, and the cached diff for that directory must also remain empty. Existing user changes must be documented rather than erased.

The implementation plan must explicitly identify any findings that appear to require changes to this protected directory and propose a safe alternative. If no safe alternative exists, report the limitation instead of violating the invariant.

### 4.2 No fabricated production data

Zero hardcoded mock data or fabricated metrics in production views.

Investigate all production-facing data displays, including:

- Candidate names and resume titles.
- ATS scores, score labels, progress indicators, and screening results.
- Job application counts, application statuses, and tracker stages.
- Job-match percentages and skill-match indicators.
- Resume completeness and section-completion percentages.
- AI insights, recommendations, bullet-strength ratings, and screening checks.
- Interview statistics, activity charts, billing figures, user metrics, and dashboard summaries.
- Dates, notifications, recent activities, and other supposedly live information.

Trace each value to its actual API response, database-backed platform state, or valid deterministic calculation engine.

Use existing engines such as `calculateAtsScore` where appropriate and verify their actual contracts before proposing integration changes. Never invent a replacement scoring formula merely to make a screen look complete.

When data is absent, loading, unavailable, or invalid, plan honest empty, loading, unavailable, or error states. Use a neutral fallback such as `—` where appropriate.

Static demonstration data is acceptable only in explicitly designated fixtures, stories, or test environments that cannot silently leak into production views.

### 4.3 Cuba Design System compliance

All proposed changes must follow the existing Cuba Design System and its established component conventions.

- Reuse existing design tokens for colour, typography, spacing, borders, shadows, radii, and states.
- Reuse approved shared components and interaction patterns.
- Do not introduce arbitrary uncurated hexadecimal colours, raw palette utilities, or independent visual systems.
- Do not create parallel components when an existing component can be correctly extended.
- Identify token gaps or component gaps explicitly rather than bypassing the design system.
- Preserve established product branding and avoid unnecessary redesigns of already-correct elements.

Inspect the actual repository implementation before concluding which tokens or components are available.

### 4.4 Preserve existing functionality

Do not sacrifice existing capabilities for visual simplicity.

Every proposed change must account for:

- Existing routes and route parameters.
- Authentication and authorisation behaviour.
- API request and response contracts.
- Form validation and submission.
- Autosave, recovery, and unsaved-change behaviour.
- Loading, error, retry, and cancellation behaviour.
- Existing keyboard and pointer interactions.
- Responsive behaviour and application-shell conventions.
- Cross-feature data consistency.

The goal is to improve the experience without breaking established platform semantics.

### 4.5 Bounded dashboard ergonomics

Preserve the existing single-viewport dashboard experience wherever the current design is intentionally bounded.

- Do not introduce unnecessary whole-window scrolling.
- Avoid nested scroll containers that trap users or hide content.
- Identify fixed-height panels, overflow clipping, sticky headers, sidebars, drawers, and responsive breakpoints.
- Distinguish intentionally scrollable content regions from actual layout defects.
- Ensure essential actions, status indicators, and navigation remain accessible.
- Verify the intended behaviour at realistic desktop, laptop, tablet, and mobile widths during the later implementation phase.

Do not impose a universal no-scroll rule on content pages that legitimately require document scrolling.

## 5. AUTHORITATIVE `/build-resume` VISUAL REFERENCE

The user's supplied resume-builder reference screenshot is an authoritative design requirement, not optional inspiration.

Locate and inspect the available reference asset, including `build-resume-target-reference.png` if present. Record its actual location and whether the complete screenshot is accessible.

If the asset is unavailable, do not fabricate a claim of pixel-level verification. Preserve the specification below and record the missing reference as an implementation-validation dependency.

### 5.1 Required page composition

**A. Application sidebar**

- Render inside the established `CubaAppShell`.
- Mark **Resumes & Master CV** as the active navigation destination.
- Preserve the established sidebar structure, iconography, spacing, active states, and responsive behaviour.

**B. Breadcrumb**

Render the following four-level hierarchy from the `xl` breakpoint upward:

`Dashboard > Resumes & Master CV > Build Resume > [Candidate Name / Resume Title]`

- The first three segments must navigate to their correct destinations.
- The first two segments are expected to resolve to `/dashboard` under the supplied specification.
- The third segment is also specified as `/dashboard` in the existing reference mandate; verify the actual route architecture and flag this unusual mapping for confirmation before implementation rather than silently inventing a route.
- The final segment represents the active resume title or candidate name and must reflect real application state.
- Do not use a hardcoded candidate name.
- Ensure the breadcrumb is hidden or adapted below `xl` according to the established responsive design without removing essential navigation.

**C. Page header**

Plan the reference composition containing:

- Active resume title.
- Green `Saved` status pill when persistence is genuinely confirmed.
- Circular ATS score gauge showing a value such as `69/100` only when supplied by real state or a valid calculation.
- Correct corresponding qualitative assessment, such as `Needs Improvement`, derived from the actual scoring rules.
- `Preview` action.
- Dark `Download` dropdown action.

Never hardcode the example score, status, or candidate name. A save indicator must reflect actual save state, not merely a completed local interaction.

**D. Horizontal stepper**

- Step index, title, and subtitle.
- Active, completed, upcoming, and error states where supported.
- Horizontal navigation consistent with the reference.
- Clear keyboard interaction, focus visibility, and responsive overflow behaviour.
- Correct synchronisation between the selected step and rendered form section.

**E. Main editing section**

Include the specified composition:

- Section heading.
- Required-field completion count, such as `5/5 required fields`, calculated from actual validation state.
- `Complete` status only when its underlying requirements are satisfied.
- `Auto Fill with AI` action.
- `Reset Section` action with appropriate confirmation or recovery behaviour.
- Photo uploader and genuine file specifications.
- Two-column input grid with appropriate icons.
- Collapsible `More details (optional)` section.
- Collapsible `Target Role & Job Description` section.
- Contextual step footer with valid previous/next navigation and applicable save state.

Inspect the actual form schema and backend validation rules before deciding which fields are required. Do not manufacture validation rules to reproduce screenshot text.

**F. Right-side AI assistant rail**

Preserve the reference's contextual right rail with:

- `Suggestions` tab.
- `Resume Insights` tab.
- `Job Match` tab.
- Screening checks.
- ATS Guidance checklist.
- Bullet Strength indicator.

Every panel must display real, contextually relevant data or a truthful empty/unavailable state. Tab switching, refresh, loading, errors, and contextual updates must be included in the planned verification.

### 5.2 Reference-parity acceptance criteria

The implementation plan must identify the components and files responsible for each of the six regions above and specify how parity will be verified.

Target exact structural and visual parity with the supplied reference wherever compatible with current architecture and explicit invariants. Dynamic data must remain dynamic; screenshot example values must never become production defaults.

## 6. MANDATORY PLATFORM-WIDE INVESTIGATION

Build an inventory from the actual source code, not from memory or a manually assumed list.

### 6.1 Routes and page coverage

Discover and classify:

- Public and marketing pages.
- Authentication, registration, password recovery, and session-related pages.
- Dashboards and role-specific workspaces.
- Resume creation, editing, preview, export, templates, and master-profile workflows.
- ATS scoring and analysis interfaces.
- Job discovery, applications, and application tracking.
- Interview preparation, live interview workflows, and AI-assisted features.
- User settings, profile management, notifications, and account controls.
- Administrative and operational interfaces.
- Billing, plans, subscriptions, invoices, and payment-related screens.
- Error pages, access-denied pages, not-found routes, and fallback views.
- Any additional routes or features discovered in the repository.

Include nested routes, route parameters, conditional routes, redirects, and route guards. Distinguish confirmed routes from inferred or unreachable routes.

### 6.2 Shared UI components

Inventory and inspect:

- Application shells and navigation.
- Headers, breadcrumbs, tabs, and stepper controls.
- Buttons, icon buttons, dropdowns, and menus.
- Modals, dialogs, drawers, popovers, and tooltips.
- Forms, field components, validation messages, and file uploaders.
- Data tables, sorting, filters, pagination, and bulk actions.
- Cards, charts, gauges, progress bars, and statistics.
- Notifications, toasts, banners, and confirmation prompts.
- Loading skeletons, empty states, error states, and retry controls.
- Responsive navigation and overflow containers.

Identify duplicated components, near-duplicates, inconsistent interaction semantics, and components with overlapping responsibilities. Propose consolidation only where safe and supported by evidence.

Explicitly investigate known components where present, including:

- `SyncProfileModal.tsx`
- `ValidationModal.tsx`
- `ShareModal.tsx`
- `StepsOverviewModal.tsx`

Do not assume these files exist at a particular path. Locate them and determine their current usage.

### 6.3 Interactive-element audit

For every relevant interactive element, trace the complete interaction path:

`User action → Event handler → State transition → API/service operation → Result → User feedback`

Inspect:

- Buttons with missing or ineffective handlers.
- Dead links and invalid navigation destinations.
- Dropdowns that do not open or execute their selected action.
- Modals that cannot close, submit, or recover properly.
- Forms that appear to submit but fail to persist data.
- Actions that silently swallow errors.
- Duplicate event handlers and conflicting state updates.
- Stale state after save, delete, refresh, or navigation.
- Inaccessible keyboard interactions.
- Incorrect disabled states.
- Missing confirmation for destructive actions.
- Missing feedback for long-running operations.
- Repeated submissions and race conditions.
- Incorrect loading, cancellation, and retry behaviour.

Classify each finding as verified, probable, or unverified. A component's visual appearance alone is not proof that its functionality is operational.

### 6.4 Frontend-to-backend completeness

For each major user-facing feature, trace:

`Route → Page → Component → State management → API client → Endpoint → Data contract → Persistence/calculation → Rendered result`

Identify:

- Backend capabilities without a usable frontend entry point.
- Frontend controls without a valid backend operation.
- Incomplete or inconsistent API integration.
- Fields present in the interface but absent from persistence contracts.
- Data that becomes stale after mutations.
- Missing loading, empty, error, and retry states.
- Permission and ownership checks that are not reflected in the UI.
- Missing pagination or inappropriate data fetching.
- Incorrect handling of partial or unavailable responses.
- Unused endpoints or orphaned components, where demonstrable.

Do not infer that a backend capability is functional simply because an endpoint or service file exists. Mark actual runtime validation as pending when it cannot be performed under Plan Mode.

## 7. VISUAL QUALITY, RESPONSIVENESS, AND ACCESSIBILITY

### 7.1 Visual consistency

Inspect:

- Alignment, spacing, hierarchy, typography, and content density.
- Inconsistent card dimensions, button sizing, and icon alignment.
- Overflow, clipping, overlapping, and truncated content.
- Misaligned grids and inconsistent column proportions.
- Modal dimensions, placement, stacking, and backdrop behaviour.
- Sticky elements and sidebar interactions.
- Visual inconsistencies across related workflows.
- Missing or inconsistent hover, focus, active, selected, disabled, success, warning, and error states.

Avoid proposing arbitrary styling changes without identifying the existing design-system implementation and the affected component.

### 7.2 Responsive behaviour

Map the existing breakpoints and inspect layout logic for:

- Large desktop displays.
- Standard laptop viewports.
- Tablet widths.
- Mobile widths.

Flag layout defects that can be established from source inspection. Mark actual cross-browser and viewport testing as pending until authorised.

Preserve bounded dashboard layouts while ensuring ordinary content pages can scroll naturally when required.

### 7.3 Accessibility

Use **WCAG 2.1 AA** as the required baseline.

Inspect and plan verification for:

- Semantic HTML and correct heading hierarchy.
- Accessible names for interactive controls.
- Unique, context-appropriate accessible labels where uniqueness is necessary.
- Keyboard navigation and visible focus indicators.
- Logical focus order and focus management in dialogs.
- Keyboard-accessible dropdowns, tabs, and steppers.
- Colour contrast for text, icons, borders, and interactive states.
- Labels and instructions for form controls.
- Programmatic association of validation errors.
- Appropriate ARIA roles and states without redundant or incorrect ARIA.
- Screen-reader announcements for save states, asynchronous updates, and errors.
- Reduced-motion preferences where animations are used.
- Accessible alternatives to colour-only status communication.

Do not add `aria-label` indiscriminately to every element. Prefer correct semantic markup, visible labels, and appropriate accessible naming. Investigate repeated IDs and duplicate accessible names that create genuine ambiguity.

## 8. DATA INTEGRITY AND STATE-MANAGEMENT AUDIT

Identify issues involving:

- Hardcoded production values and example data leaking into real views.
- Incorrect derived metrics and inconsistent scoring calculations.
- Missing or inconsistent loading and empty states.
- Race conditions and stale closures.
- Unhandled rejected promises.
- State desynchronisation between the editor, preview, sidebar, and AI assistant.
- Autosave timing, save confirmation, and recovery.
- Unsaved changes when navigating between routes.
- Form reset behaviour and accidental data loss.
- Optimistic updates without rollback.
- Duplicate requests or duplicate submissions.
- Pagination, filtering, and sorting inconsistencies.
- Invalid, null, missing, or malformed API fields.
- Timezone, date-formatting, and number-formatting inconsistencies.

Trace existing calculations and state transitions before proposing changes. Prefer shared, deterministic domain logic over duplicated UI-specific calculations.

Any future destructive or reset operation must preserve clear user intent, appropriate confirmation, and recovery expectations.

## 9. TEST STRATEGY AND ACCEPTANCE REQUIREMENTS

Plan a layered validation programme for the subsequent implementation phase.

### Layer 1 — Static and repository validation

- Production build must exit with code `0`.
- ESLint must exit with zero errors.
- Existing formatting, type-checking, and test conventions must be respected.
- No unintended dependency or configuration changes.
- No changes to `src/cv-templates/`.

Inspect the package scripts and current toolchain before specifying exact commands. Do not invent scripts that do not exist.

### Layer 2 — Component and integration testing

- Form validation and submission.
- Save, autosave, reset, and recovery.
- Dialogs, drawers, tabs, menus, and steppers.
- API success, empty, loading, error, and retry states.
- Real-data binding and derived metric correctness.
- Route transitions and permission-aware behaviour.

### Layer 3 — Browser end-to-end testing

Plan realistic user journeys through the major platform features, including resume creation and editing, preview/download, ATS analysis, job tracking, AI assistance, and any other workflows confirmed to exist.

Use the existing browser test infrastructure where available. Identify infrastructure dependencies and distinguish planned coverage from tests actually executed.

### Layer 4 — Accessibility and responsive validation

- Keyboard-only interaction.
- Automated accessibility checks.
- Manual semantic and focus-management review.
- Contrast validation.
- Representative viewport testing.
- Regression checks for bounded dashboards and nested scrolling.

### Layer 5 — Regression and release evidence

- Existing tests continue to pass.
- No previously operational feature becomes inaccessible or broken.
- API contracts and persistence semantics remain compatible.
- Protected directories remain untouched.
- Visual comparisons use the supplied reference where available.
- All critical and high-priority findings receive explicit closure evidence.

**Definition of success:** Build and lint requirements are satisfied, all release-blocking defects are resolved and verified, relevant journeys operate correctly, no production view fabricates platform data, the design system is respected, accessibility and responsive checks have evidence, and no protected invariant is violated.

Do not claim that these outcomes have been achieved by submitting a plan.

## 10. REQUIRED FORENSIC DELIVERABLES

The plan must identify the following evidence artefacts to produce during the authorised implementation phase, using existing documentation conventions and non-conflicting paths:

1. **UI/UX Architecture Inventory** — route hierarchy, layouts, shared components, design-system dependencies, and component ownership.
2. **Backend-to-UI Completeness Matrix** — feature, frontend entry point, service/API dependency, data source, integration status, and verified gaps.
3. **UI/UX Defect Register** — unique finding ID, severity, affected route, file and symbol references, evidence, impact, proposed remedy, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
4. **Interaction and User-Journey Matrix** — user actions, expected outcomes, error recovery, permissions, and testing requirements.
5. **Accessibility and Responsive Audit Matrix** — applicable requirements, affected components, known evidence, and planned validation.
6. **`/build-resume` Reference-Parity Plan** — reference availability, six-region mapping, component ownership, dynamic-data requirements, and visual acceptance criteria.
7. **Implementation and Regression-Test Plan** — dependency-aware execution sequence, risk controls, test coverage, and release gates.
8. **Final UI/UX Completeness Report** — verified fixes, unresolved issues, deferred work, test evidence, and remaining production risks, to be produced only after implementation and verification.

These are planned deliverables, not permission to create or modify files now. Existing documents should be inspected first to avoid duplicate or conflicting artefacts.

## 11. SEVERITY, PRIORITISATION, AND IMPLEMENTATION SEQUENCING

Assign every finding a unique ID and a risk-based priority.

- **P0 — Critical:** Security or authorisation exposure, material data corruption or loss, severe production blockers, or critical failures in essential user journeys.
- **P1 — High:** Major feature failures, broken core workflows, fabricated production metrics, severe accessibility barriers, or widespread navigation defects.
- **P2 — Medium:** Material usability, responsive-layout, interaction, or visual-consistency defects that do not qualify as P0/P1.
- **P3 — Low:** Minor polish, non-blocking inconsistencies, and lower-impact refinements.

The directive's overall priority remains P0. Individual findings must receive their own evidence-based severity rather than all being labelled P0.

For each finding, include:

- User and business impact.
- Reproduction or source-evidence details.
- Affected files, components, routes, and contracts.
- Root cause, where verified.
- Proposed correction.
- Dependency and regression risk.
- Acceptance criteria.
- Planned verification method.
- Estimated complexity or effort, clearly labelled as an estimate.
- Any unresolved decision requiring owner approval.

Organise the proposed work into logical, dependency-aware waves:

1. Repository baseline, protected-invariant controls, and investigation completion.
2. Critical data-integrity, navigation, and workflow failures.
3. Shared application-shell and design-system inconsistencies.
4. Core feature pages and component-level defects.
5. Resume-builder reference parity.
6. Accessibility, responsive behaviour, and interaction completeness.
7. Cross-feature integration, edge cases, and regression coverage.
8. Release validation, evidence collection, and final audit.

Reorder these waves when repository evidence shows a more appropriate dependency sequence. Do not assume that all features are equally broken or require a rewrite.

## 12. REQUIRED FINAL PLAN RESPONSE

Before submitting the plan, assemble a concise but technically complete report containing:

1. **Workspace verification:** expected path, actual path, repository identity, branch, HEAD, and working-tree state.
2. **Investigation coverage:** routes, components, services, configuration, and tests actually inspected.
3. **Evidence-backed findings:** severity, impact, file/symbol references, and verified versus unverified status.
4. **Critical invariants:** confirmation of the intended protection strategy for `src/cv-templates/`, production data integrity, Cuba tokens, and dashboard ergonomics.
5. **Reference-parity findings:** available screenshot status, affected components, and any unresolved route or design ambiguities.
6. **Implementation waves:** ordered actions, dependencies, and measurable acceptance criteria.
7. **Verification matrix:** build, lint, component tests, integration tests, browser journeys, accessibility, responsiveness, and regression validation.
8. **Risks and blockers:** missing assets, unavailable environments, unclear contracts, test-infrastructure limitations, and decisions requiring approval.
9. **Explicit exclusions:** all implementation, file modification, build-artifact generation, and state-changing operations remain unauthorised.
10. **Bridge submission evidence:** the exact plan-submission command and its actual result.

Do not present assumptions as facts. Use the following evidence classifications:

- **Verified:** supported by direct repository evidence or an actually executed, permitted check.
- **Probable:** strongly indicated by source evidence but not confirmed in runtime behaviour.
- **Unverified:** requires an authorised runtime, browser, backend, or external-system check.
- **Blocked:** cannot be investigated or validated with currently available access or assets.

If coverage is incomplete, explicitly report what remains uninspected. Do not claim a comprehensive audit is complete merely because a route or component inventory was generated.

## 13. MANDATORY BRIDGE PLAN SUBMISSION

**You must execute the following terminal command to submit the plan. A chat-only response is not sufficient.**

After the read-only investigation is complete, construct a concise summary and a semicolon-delimited step list based on the actual findings.

Execute the equivalent of:

```powershell
bridge dev plan --directive DIR-093 --projectDir "D:\xampp\htdocs\IME365" --summary "<Evidence-based plan summary>" --steps "<Step 1>;<Step 2>;<Step 3>;<Step 4>;<Step 5>"
```

Replace the example placeholders with the real summary and implementation steps. Escape or quote shell arguments correctly. Do not place unescaped embedded quotation marks in arguments.

The summary must communicate that DIR-093 is a read-only forensic UI/UX audit and that implementation is not authorised.

The steps should capture the main evidence-backed implementation waves, their dependencies, and the required verification gates. Keep the command concise enough for reliable terminal execution.

### Bridge command handling

- Verify that the Bridge CLI is available using a non-mutating check where possible.
- Do not invent a successful submission response.
- If the command is unavailable, fails, or requires additional permissions, preserve the failure output and report the exact blocker.
- Do not attempt undocumented Bridge commands or change the project to work around a submission failure.
- A command invocation alone is not proof of success; inspect and report the actual exit status and returned result.
- If submission fails, do not claim that the plan was submitted.

## 14. FINAL EXECUTIVE INSTRUCTION

Investigate first. Build the evidence register. Map dependencies. Identify the smallest safe corrections that can achieve the intended quality. Define objective acceptance criteria. Submit the plan through Bridge.

**Do not modify a single project file during DIR-093 Plan Mode.**

Do not skip inconvenient routes, assume visual correctness from component existence, treat a rendered button as a working action, or confuse a successful build with a complete product.

Preserve all existing user work. Protect `src/cv-templates/`. Eliminate fabricated production data through verified data-source planning. Enforce Cuba Design System compliance. Preserve bounded dashboard ergonomics. Retain every legitimate platform capability.

The final result of this directive must be an actionable, auditable, risk-ranked plan that a developer can execute without guessing what to inspect, what to fix, why it matters, or how success will be proven.

**Required terminal submission:** `bridge dev plan --directive DIR-093 --projectDir "D:\xampp\htdocs\IME365" --summary "<Plan summary>" --steps "<Step 1>;<Step 2>;<Step 3>"`

**Authorisation boundary:** Plan Mode only. Wait for explicit implementation authorisation before making any changes.
invariants: Zero modifications to src/cv-templates/ (git diff must remain exactly 0 bytes).
Zero hardcoded mock data or fabricated metrics; all reads bind to real platform state.
Strict Cuba Design System token compliance (no arbitrary uncurated hex or raw palette utilities).
Single-viewport ergonomics preserved (no whole-window scroll regression on bounded dashboards).
All interactive elements remain 100% operational with zero dead buttons, dead routes, or duplicate components.
WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility compliance (unique aria-labels, focus rings, contrast ratios).
Production build (npm run build) must exit 0 and ESLint must exit 0 errors.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: End-to-End Surface Audit & Enhancement: Candidate dashboard (Overview, Resumes, Cover Letters, Portfolios, Jobs, Applications, Interview, Messages, Settings), Public pages (Landing, Pricing, Templates, FAQs, Blog, Jobs), and Global Navigation chrome are 100% upgraded to Cuba Modern Executive styling.

AC2: Visual Layout Blueprint in Plan: Plan includes structured visual page layouts and component hierarchy mappings across mobile (375px), tablet (768px), desktop (1280px), and wide (1440px+) viewports.
AC3: 100% Operational Integrity: All controls, filters, modals, drawer triggers, command palette actions, and navigation paths are proven operational with zero dead links or orphan states.
AC4: Zero Redundancy & Deduplication: All duplicated cards, duplicated metric calls, repeated headlines, and redundant markup are eliminated across all touched surfaces.
AC5: Cuba Token & Glassmorphism Parity: Unified glassmorphism tokens, border lines, subtle shadows, and hover micro-animations applied consistently with zero raw hex or uncurated utility overrides.

AC6: Automated Verification & Certification: Comprehensive test suites pass (all existing regression suites + new visual/DOM parity assertions), Playwright DOM interactive census verified with zero console errors, Vite build exits 0, and src/cv-templates/ remains 100% frozen.
